item.research_question: Can a HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy coating produced by electrospark deposition provide high corrosion resistance in aggressive saline environments compared to a stainless steel substrate?
item.material_system: HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (equiatomic composition) deposited on 316 stainless steel substrate
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying of high-purity Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr powders for 60 h in a planetary ball mill with n-heptane as process control agent; consolidation via spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C, 50 MPa, and 100 hPa vacuum; electrospark deposition using Spark Depo Model 3 equipment under argon atmosphere
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical testing in 3.5% NaCl saline solution at room temperature; Open Circuit Potential (Eoc) measured for 6 h; Potentiodynamic polarization from −0.2 to +0.2 V at 1 mV/s scanning rate; Vickers hardness measured with 0.98 N load
key_findings: The sintered bulk material achieved a density of 8.96 g/cm³, representing approximately 90% of the theoretical density of 9.9 g/cm³.
The deposited coating had a thickness of approximately 20 μm with a compact structure and no cracks at the interface.
The bulk consolidated sample exhibited a Vickers hardness of 840 HV.
The coating showed a corrosion rate of 0.00024 mm/year in 3.5% NaCl solution.
The coating demonstrated a more electropositive corrosion potential and lower corrosion current density compared to 316 stainless steel (icorr of 12.53 µA/cm²).
XRD analysis confirmed the main phase as body-centered cubic (BCC) with some very small FCC peaks in the coating.
Fine fissures were observed on the coating surface due to rapid cooling, but they did not penetrate the interface or significantly affect corrosion resistance.
item.mechanism: The high configurational entropy and specific thermodynamic parameters (Ω ≥ 1.1, δ ≤ 6.6, VEC = 4.4) favor the formation of a stable BCC solid solution. The electrospark deposition process, performed under an argon atmosphere, produces high-purity coatings with low oxygen concentration. The rapid cooling during deposition causes fine surface fissures, but the compact nature of the layer and the formation of a passivation film (confirmed by oxygen presence in EDS) ensure good adhesion and corrosion resistance despite the thin film and minor cracks.
item.limitations: The coating thickness was limited to approximately 20 μm, which could influence corrosion resistance; fine fissures are present on the surface due to rapid cooling and high hardness; the study was limited to 3.5% NaCl solution and did not test other aggressive media.
item.future_work: Future work will focus on optimizing electrospark deposition parameters to reduce cracking, depositing thicker layers, and testing in other chlorine-containing fluids such as geothermal fluids and in situ geothermal environments.
quotes: The corrosion rate obtained after a test in chlorine containing fluid was very small (0.00024 mm/year)
The coating was thin (approx. 20 μm), and the corrosion resistance could have been influenced by the coating thickness.
The cracks, however, are not present in the coating structure, as they can be observed in the cross section.
